source_note: Iron meteorites are core fragments of differentiated asteroids — >95% Fe-Ni metal. Mittlefehldt et al. 1998.
Stony-iron: ~50% Fe-Ni metal matrix with olivine crystals. Boesenberg & Delaney 1997.
Stony-iron breccia: ~45-50% Fe-Ni metal mixed with silicate clasts. Mittlefehldt 1998.
Ordinary chondrite, High-iron: 15-19% free Fe-Ni metal. Jarosewich 1990.
Ordinary chondrite, Low-iron: 4-10% free Fe-Ni metal. Jarosewich 1990.
Ordinary chondrite, Low-Low-iron: 1-3% free Fe-Ni metal. Jarosewich 1990.
Ordinary chondrite, ambiguous classification (e.g. H/L, L/LL). Midpoint of bracketing classes.
Ordinary chondrite without group assignment (recclass='OC'). Treated as L-equivalent.
Enstatite chondrite, High-iron. Formed in very reducing nebular conditions. Keil 1989.
Enstatite chondrite, Low-iron. Keil 1989.
Enstatite chondrite, group not specified. Midpoint of EH/EL.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Ivuna-type. Fully aqueously altered, no free metal. Brearley & Jones 1998.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Mighei-type. Trace metal + magnetite. Brearley & Jones 1998.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Ornans-type. Small chondrules with minor metal.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Vigarano-type. Mostly silicate with magnetite.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Karoonda-type. Highly oxidized, minimal free metal.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Renazzo-type. Notably metal-rich for a CC. Krot et al. 2002.
Carbonaceous chondrite, ALH 85085-like. Unusually metal-rich (~20%). Bischoff et al. 1993.
Carbonaceous chondrite, Bencubbinite. ~60-70% Fe-Ni metal — an outlier among CCs. Weisberg et al. 2001.
Carbonaceous chondrite, ungrouped. Conservative low estimate since most CCs are metal-poor.
Rumuruti chondrite. Highly oxidized; almost no free metal. Schulze et al. 1994.
Kakangari chondrite. Rare type with moderate metal content (~6-8%). Weisberg et al. 1996.
Chondrite not assignable to a specific group. Conservative midrange estimate.
Lunar meteorite — Moon is differentiated, crust/regolith has essentially no free Fe-Ni metal.
Martian meteorite (shergottite/nakhlite/chassignite). Mars is differentiated.
Basaltic achondrite from Vesta's crust. Metal sank to Vesta's core.
Ultramafic achondrite from Vesta's mantle. No free metal.
Brecciated eucrite-diogenite mix from Vesta. No free metal.
Carbon-rich ultramafic achondrite with trace metal grains. Goodrich 1992.
Enstatite achondrite. Highly reduced but mostly metal-stripped.
Basaltic achondrite, distinct from HEDs. No free metal.
Primitive achondrite — partially melted, retains some metal. McCoy et al. 1996.
Primitive achondrite, higher degree of melting than acapulcoites but more residual metal.
Primitive achondrite. IAB iron parent body relative.
Olivine-rich primitive achondrite. Trace metal.
Achondrite of unspecified type. Differentiated → conservative low estimate.
Recclass that does not match any known group (e.g. 'Stone-uncl', 'Fusion crust', 'Unknown'). Weight 0 to avoid overstating yield.
